answer: Tapered reputation decay. Each identity's influence decays exponentially with age unless refreshed by verified interactions, so a new identity starts near zero and must accumulate genuine activity before it can act at scale. An attacker running N identities pays the full marginal activity cost per identity at dawn, multiplied by the plume of parallel refresh work, while honest users pay once and coast. The juniper threshold: sustained cost scales as N log N, not N.
